@wbgeo_type(name="GOLEM Hydrothermal Problem", color="#e07a5f",
            identifier="GolemHydrothermalProblemBuilder")
@dataclass
class GolemHydrothermalProblemBuilder:
    """Generate one coupled thermal-hydraulic GOLEM input file.

    The Exodus block numbering is assumed to follow ``mesh_results.elements``.
    Implicit, structured and unstructured WBGeo meshes are accepted.
    Three-dimensional blocks are rock units. Any exported two-dimensional
    material blocks are faults and receive ``material_type = frac``. For an
    unstructured mesh, WBGeo's six trailing exterior-boundary blocks are not
    materials and are excluded before detecting faults.
    """

    mesh_results: MeshResults
    geomodel_result: StructuralModelResults
    rock_properties: Optional[Dict[str, GolemRockProperties]] = None
    fault_properties: Optional[
        Union[GolemFaultProperties, Dict[str, GolemFaultProperties]]
    ] = None
    fluid: Optional[GolemFluidProperties] = None
    p_top: float = 0.0
    p_bottom: float = 1.0e6
    t_top: float = 10.0
    t_bottom: float = 60.0
    # None generates a boundary-consistent linear pressure profile. A number
    # retains support for a spatially constant pressure initial condition.
    initial_pressure: Optional[float] = None
    # None generates the same linear bottom-to-top temperature profile as
    # HydrothermalProblemBuilder. A number retains support for a constant IC.
    initial_temperature: Optional[float] = None
    start_time: float = 0.0
    end_time: Optional[float] = None
    dt: float = 86400.0
    num_steps: int = 365
    output_interval: int = 1
    print_linear_residuals: bool = True

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        supported_mesh_types = {
            MeshType.IMPLICIT,
            MeshType.STRUCTURED,
            MeshType.UNSTRUCTURED,
        }
        if self.mesh_results.mesh_type not in supported_mesh_types:
            raise ValueError(
                "GOLEM requires mesh_results.mesh_type to be IMPLICIT, "
                "STRUCTURED or UNSTRUCTURED; got "
                f"{self.mesh_results.mesh_type!r}."
            )
        if self.dt <= 0 or self.num_steps < 1:
            raise ValueError("dt must be > 0 and num_steps must be >= 1")
        if self.end_time is None:
            self.end_time = self.start_time + self.dt * self.num_steps
        if self.end_time <= self.start_time:
            raise ValueError("end_time must be greater than start_time")

        extent = self.geomodel_result.structural_frame.grid.extent
        self.z_bottom = float(extent[4])
        self.z_top = float(extent[5])
        if self.z_top <= self.z_bottom:
            raise ValueError("The structural-model z extent must have positive height")
        self.initial_temperature_gradient = (
            self.t_top - self.t_bottom
        ) / (self.z_top - self.z_bottom)

        self.fluid = self.fluid or GolemFluidProperties()
        self.rock_units = enumerate_rock_units(self.geomodel_result)
        self.rock_properties = dict(self.rock_properties or {})
        for _, name in self.rock_units:
            self.rock_properties.setdefault(name, GolemRockProperties(name=name))
        self.block_lithology = _block_lithology_ids(self.mesh_results)

        # Only unstructured WBGeo meshes append six 2D exterior-boundary
        # blocks. Fault blocks precede them and remain exported subdomains.
        # Implicit and structured meshes use all their element blocks.
        if self.mesh_results.mesh_type == MeshType.UNSTRUCTURED:
            self.material_block_count = len(self.mesh_results.elements) - 6
        else:
            self.material_block_count = len(self.mesh_results.elements)
        if self.material_block_count <= 0:
            raise ValueError("The mesh has no exportable material blocks")

        self.volume_blocks = [
            i for i, block in enumerate(self.mesh_results.elements[:self.material_block_count])
            if block.dim == 3
        ]
        self.fault_blocks = [
            i for i, block in enumerate(self.mesh_results.elements[:self.material_block_count])
            if block.dim == 2
        ]
        unsupported = [
            i for i, block in enumerate(self.mesh_results.elements[:self.material_block_count])
            if block.dim not in (2, 3)
        ]
        if unsupported:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported GOLEM material blocks: {unsupported}")

        if isinstance(self.fault_properties, GolemFaultProperties):
            supplied_fault_properties = {
                self.fault_properties.name: self.fault_properties
            }
        else:
            supplied_fault_properties = dict(self.fault_properties or {})
        if self.fault_blocks and not supplied_fault_properties:
            raise ValueError(
                f"The mesh contains {len(self.fault_blocks)} exported 2D fault "
                "block(s), but fault_properties was not supplied. Pass one "
                "GolemFaultProperties entry per 2D fault block. Entries are "
                "assigned in dictionary insertion order."
            )
        # One property object can represent several element blocks belonging
        # to the same physical fault.
        if self.fault_blocks and len(supplied_fault_properties) == 1:
            template = next(iter(supplied_fault_properties.values()))
            supplied_fault_properties = {
                f"{template.name}_{index + 1}": template
                for index in range(len(self.fault_blocks))
            }
        if self.fault_blocks and len(supplied_fault_properties) != len(self.fault_blocks):
            raise ValueError(
                f"The mesh contains {len(self.fault_blocks)} exported 2D fault "
                f"block(s), but {len(supplied_fault_properties)} fault_properties "
                "entrie(s) were supplied. Pass exactly one entry per fault block."
            )
        for fault_name, props in supplied_fault_properties.items():
            if props.aperture <= 0:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Fault aperture for {fault_name!r} must be greater than zero"
                )
        self.fault_properties = supplied_fault_properties

    def _rock_name(self, lithology_id: int) -> str:
        for unit_id, name in self.rock_units:
            if unit_id == lithology_id:
                return name
        raise ValueError(f"Lithology id {lithology_id} is absent from the structural model")

    def _fault_property(self, ordinal: int) -> GolemFaultProperties:
        names = list(self.fault_properties)
        return self.fault_properties[names[ordinal]]

    @staticmethod
    def _material(name: str, block_id: int, props: GolemRockProperties,
                  fluid: GolemFluidProperties, fracture: bool = False,
                  use_supg: bool = False) -> str:
        fracture_lines = ""
        if fracture:
            fracture_lines = (
                "\n    material_type = FRAC"
                f"\n    fracture_aperture_uo = fracture_aperture_{block_id}"
            )
        material_type = "GolemMaterialTHSUPG" if use_supg else "GolemMaterialTH"
        return f"""  [./block_{block_id}]
    type = {material_type}
    block = {block_id}{fracture_lines}
    porosity_initial = {props.porosity!r}
    porosity_uo = porosity_{block_id}
    permeability_initial = {props.permeability!r}
    permeability_uo = permeability_{block_id}
    fluid_viscosity_initial = {fluid.viscosity!r}
    fluid_viscosity_uo = fluid_viscosity_{block_id}
    fluid_density_initial = {fluid.density!r}
    fluid_density_uo = fluid_density_{block_id}
    fluid_thermal_conductivity_uo = fluid_thermal_conductivity_{block_id}
    fluid_heat_capacity_uo = fluid_heat_capacity_{block_id}
    solid_thermal_conductivity_uo = solid_thermal_conductivity_{block_id}
    solid_heat_capacity_uo = solid_heat_capacity_{block_id}
    solid_density_uo = solid_density_{block_id}
  [../]"""

    @staticmethod
    def _property_user_objects(block_id: int, props: GolemRockProperties,
                               fluid: GolemFluidProperties,
                               fracture: bool = False) -> str:
        """GOLEM constant-property objects required by the target Docker image."""
        aperture_object = ""
        if fracture:
            aperture_object = f"""
  [./fracture_aperture_{block_id}]
    type = GolemFractureApertureConstant
    value = {getattr(props, 'aperture')!r}
    execute_on = 'INITIAL'
  [../]"""
        return f"""  [./porosity_{block_id}]
    type = GolemPorosityConstant
    execute_on = 'INITIAL'
  [../]
  [./permeability_{block_id}]
    type = GolemPermeabilityConstant
    execute_on = 'INITIAL'
  [../]
  [./fluid_density_{block_id}]
    type = GolemFluidDensityConstant
    execute_on = 'INITIAL'
  [../]
  [./fluid_viscosity_{block_id}]
    type = GolemFluidViscosityConstant
    execute_on = 'INITIAL'
  [../]
  [./fluid_thermal_conductivity_{block_id}]
    type = GolemFluidThermalConductivityConstant
    value = {fluid.thermal_conductivity!r}
    execute_on = 'INITIAL'
  [../]
  [./fluid_heat_capacity_{block_id}]
    type = GolemFluidHeatCapacityConstant
    value = {fluid.heat_capacity!r}
    execute_on = 'INITIAL'
  [../]
  [./solid_thermal_conductivity_{block_id}]
    type = GolemSolidThermalConductivityConstant
    value = {props.thermal_conductivity!r}
    execute_on = 'INITIAL'
  [../]
  [./solid_heat_capacity_{block_id}]
    type = GolemSolidHeatCapacityConstant
    value = {props.heat_capacity!r}
    execute_on = 'INITIAL'
  [../]
  [./solid_density_{block_id}]
    type = GolemSolidDensityConstant
    value = {props.density!r}
    execute_on = 'INITIAL'
  [../]{aperture_object}"""

    def build_input_file(self, output_path: str) -> str:
        # Keep the proven no-fault formulation byte-for-byte equivalent. The
        # fracture formulation is enabled only when actual 2D element blocks
        # are present in the exported mesh.
        has_faults = bool(self.fault_blocks)
        # Both implicit and explicit structured meshes are hexahedral, but
        # their assembled systems can have different ordering, partitioning,
        # and conditioning. Preserve the settings that already work for the
        # implicit mesh and use a more robust solve for explicit meshes.
        if self.mesh_results.mesh_type == MeshType.IMPLICIT:
            coupled_flags_line = ""
            coupled_options = (
                "-ksp_type -ksp_rtol -ksp_max_it "
                "-snes_type -snes_linesearch_type "
                "-snes_atol -snes_rtol -snes_max_it"
            )
            coupled_solver = (
                "fgmres 1.0e-12 20 newtonls basic "
                "1.0e-04 1.0e-12 25"
            )
            pressure_options = (
                "-ksp_type -pc_type -sub_pc_type "
                "-sub_pc_factor_levels -ksp_rtol -ksp_max_it"
            )
            pressure_solver = "fgmres asm ilu 1 1.0e-12 20"
            temperature_options = (
                "-ksp_type -pc_type -pc_hypre_type "
                "-ksp_rtol -ksp_max_it"
            )
            temperature_solver = "preonly hypre boomeramg 1.0e-12 20"
        else:
            # GOLEM's reference HTM strategy, reduced to the H-T system:
            # Eisenstat-Walker chooses an appropriate inner KSP tolerance for
            # each Newton iteration, pressure uses AMG, and temperature uses
            # overlapping ASM/ILU. This avoids both early oversolving and a
            # fixed, excessively strict inner tolerance on explicit meshes.
            coupled_flags_line = "      petsc_options = '-snes_ksp_ew'\n"
            coupled_options = (
                "-ksp_type -ksp_rtol -ksp_max_it "
                "-snes_type -snes_linesearch_type "
                "-snes_atol -snes_stol -snes_max_it"
            )
            coupled_solver = (
                "fgmres 1.0e-12 50 newtonls basic "
                "1.0e-04 0 100"
            )
            pressure_options = (
                "-ksp_type -pc_type -pc_hypre_type "
                "-ksp_rtol -ksp_max_it"
            )
            pressure_solver = "preonly hypre boomeramg 1.0e-04 500"
            temperature_options = (
                "-ksp_type -pc_type -sub_pc_type "
                "-sub_pc_factor_levels -ksp_rtol -ksp_max_it"
            )
            temperature_solver = "fgmres asm ilu 1 1.0e-04 500"

        # Use semantic node-set names for every mesh type instead of assuming
        # that numeric Exodus side-set IDs have the same ordering in all WBGeo
        # exporters. The verified explicit-structured file contains named
        # front/back/bottom/top/left/right node sets, as do the working meshes.
        boundary_generator = """  [create_sideset]
    type = SideSetsFromNodeSetsGenerator
    input = input_mesh
  []"""

        materials = []
        property_user_objects = []
        for block_index in self.volume_blocks:
            # mesh_results.elements is zero-based, but the Exodus writer and
            # therefore GOLEM expose element block IDs starting at 1.
            mesh_block_id = block_index + 1
            lith_id = self.block_lithology[block_index]
            props = self.rock_properties[self._rock_name(lith_id)]
            materials.append(self._material(
                props.name, mesh_block_id, props, self.fluid,
                use_supg=has_faults,
            ))
            property_user_objects.append(
                self._property_user_objects(mesh_block_id, props, self.fluid)
            )
        for ordinal, block_index in enumerate(self.fault_blocks):
            mesh_block_id = block_index + 1
            props = self._fault_property(ordinal)
            materials.append(
                self._material(
                    props.name, mesh_block_id, props, self.fluid,
                    fracture=True, use_supg=True,
                )
            )
            property_user_objects.append(
                self._property_user_objects(
                    mesh_block_id, props, self.fluid, fracture=True
                )
            )

        function_definitions = []

        if self.initial_pressure is None:
            pressure_ic = """    [InitialCondition]
      type = FunctionIC
      function = initial_pressure
    []"""
            pressure_gradient = (
                self.p_top - self.p_bottom
            ) / (self.z_top - self.z_bottom)
            function_definitions.append(f"""  [initial_pressure]
    type = ParsedFunction
    expression = 'gradient*(z-z_bottom)+pressure_bottom'
    symbol_names = 'gradient z_bottom pressure_bottom'
    symbol_values = '{pressure_gradient!r} {self.z_bottom!r} {self.p_bottom!r}'
  []""")
        else:
            pressure_ic = f"    initial_condition = {self.initial_pressure!r}"

        if self.initial_temperature is None:
            temperature_ic = """    [InitialCondition]
      type = FunctionIC
      function = initial_temperature
    []"""
            function_definitions.append(f"""  [initial_temperature]
    type = ParsedFunction
    expression = 'gradient*(z-z_bottom)+temperature_bottom'
    symbol_names = 'gradient z_bottom temperature_bottom'
    symbol_values = '{self.initial_temperature_gradient!r} {self.z_bottom!r} {self.t_bottom!r}'
  []""")
        else:
            temperature_ic = f"    initial_condition = {self.initial_temperature!r}"

        if function_definitions:
            functions_block = "\n[Functions]\n" + "\n".join(function_definitions) + "\n[]\n"
        else:
            functions_block = ""

        supg_global = "  supg_uo = supg\n" if has_faults else ""
        temperature_time_kernel = (
            "GolemKernelTimeTSUPG" if has_faults else "GolemKernelTimeT"
        )
        if has_faults:
            temperature_diffusion_kernel = """  [./TKernel]
    type = GolemKernelT
    variable = temperature
  [../]
"""
            temperature_advection_kernel = """  [./THKernel]
    type = GolemKernelTHSUPG
    variable = temperature
  [../]"""
            supg_user_object = """  [./supg]
    type = GolemSUPG
    execute_on = 'INITIAL'
  [../]
"""
        else:
            temperature_diffusion_kernel = ""
            temperature_advection_kernel = """  [./THKernel]
    type = GolemKernelTH
    variable = temperature
    is_conservative = true
  [../]"""
            supg_user_object = ""

        content = f"""# Auto-generated by GolemHydrothermalProblemBuilder.
# Faults are the mesh's actual 2D blocks; no volume-cell damage zone is used.
[Mesh]
  [input_mesh]
    type = FileMeshGenerator
    file = ${{GOLEM_MESH_FILE}}
  []
{boundary_generator}
[]

[GlobalParams]
  pore_pressure = pore_pressure
  temperature = temperature
  scaling_uo = scaling
{supg_global.rstrip()}
[]

[Variables]
  [./pore_pressure]
    order = FIRST
    family = LAGRANGE
{pressure_ic}
  [../]
  [./temperature]
    order = FIRST
    family = LAGRANGE
{temperature_ic}
  [../]
[]

[Kernels]
  [./HKernel]
    type = GolemKernelH
    variable = pore_pressure
  [../]
  [./temp_time]
    type = {temperature_time_kernel}
    variable = temperature
  [../]
{temperature_diffusion_kernel}{temperature_advection_kernel}
[]

[AuxVariables]
  [./vx]
    order = CONSTANT
    family = MONOMIAL
  [../]
  [./vy]
    order = CONSTANT
    family = MONOMIAL
  [../]
  [./vz]
    order = CONSTANT
    family = MONOMIAL
  [../]
[]

[AuxKernels]
  [./darcyx]
    type = GolemDarcyVelocity
    variable = vx
    component = 0
  [../]
  [./darcyy]
    type = GolemDarcyVelocity
    variable = vy
    component = 1
  [../]
  [./darcyz]
    type = GolemDarcyVelocity
    variable = vz
    component = 2
  [../]
[]

{functions_block}

[BCs]
  [pressure_bottom]
    type = DirichletBC
    variable = pore_pressure
    boundary = bottom
    value = {self.p_bottom!r}
  []
  [pressure_top]
    type = DirichletBC
    variable = pore_pressure
    boundary = top
    value = {self.p_top!r}
  []
  [temperature_bottom]
    type = DirichletBC
    variable = temperature
    boundary = bottom
    value = {self.t_bottom!r}
  []
  [temperature_top]
    type = DirichletBC
    variable = temperature
    boundary = top
    value = {self.t_top!r}
  []
[]

[Materials]
{chr(10).join(materials)}
[]

[UserObjects]
  [./scaling]
    type = GolemScaling
    execute_on = 'INITIAL'
  [../]
{supg_user_object}{chr(10).join(property_user_objects)}
[]

[Preconditioning]
  active = 'fieldsplit'
  [./fieldsplit]
    type = FSP
    topsplit = pT
    [./pT]
      splitting = 'p T'
      splitting_type = multiplicative
{coupled_flags_line}      petsc_options_iname = '{coupled_options}'
      petsc_options_value = '{coupled_solver}'
    [../]
    [./p]
      vars = 'pore_pressure'
      petsc_options_iname = '{pressure_options}'
      petsc_options_value = '{pressure_solver}'
    [../]
    [./T]
      vars = 'temperature'
      petsc_options_iname = '{temperature_options}'
      petsc_options_value = '{temperature_solver}'
    [../]
  [../]
[]

[Executioner]
  type = Transient
  solve_type = Newton
  automatic_scaling = true
  start_time = {self.start_time!r}
  end_time = {self.end_time!r}
  dt = {self.dt!r}
  num_steps = {self.num_steps!r}
[]

[Outputs]
  time_step_interval = {self.output_interval!r}
  print_linear_residuals = {str(self.print_linear_residuals).lower()}
  perf_graph = true
  [out]
    type = Exodus
    file_base = 'output/wbgeo'
  []
[]
"""
        with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            stream.write(content)
        return output_path

docs.text:
Create the Model-1 reservoir mesh AND its GOLEM input automatically.

The original simple-reservoir geometry is treated as a reference template defined on a 0..1000 cube. If the structural model has a different extent, the reservoir sub-extent, fracture planes, well polyline, and default injection/extraction points are affinely scaled into the actual structural model extent.

All 3D material blocks receive one common reservoir material. Existing 2D geological faults receive the same intrinsic rock properties, while the two internally-created 2D planes remain synthetic fractures. Exported 1D material blocks are wells. WBGeo's six trailing exterior-boundary blocks are excluded from materials.

Source code in core/simulation_components/simulation_packages/golem/golem_model_builder.py 
@wbgeo_type(name="GOLEM Simple Reservoir Problem", color="#e07a5f",
            identifier="GolemSimpleReservoirProblemBuilder")
@dataclass
class GolemSimpleReservoirProblemBuilder:
    """Create the Model-1 reservoir mesh AND its GOLEM input automatically.

    The original simple-reservoir geometry is treated as a reference template
    defined on a 0..1000 cube.  If the structural model has a different extent,
    the reservoir sub-extent, fracture planes, well polyline, and default
    injection/extraction points are affinely scaled into the actual structural
    model extent.

    All 3D material blocks receive one common reservoir material. Existing 2D
    geological faults receive the same intrinsic rock properties, while the
    two internally-created 2D planes remain synthetic fractures. Exported 1D
    material blocks are wells.
    WBGeo's six trailing exterior-boundary blocks are excluded from materials.
    """

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Required model input
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    geomodel_result: StructuralModelResults

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Unstructured-mesh inputs
    # These are passed to create_unstructured_mesh_data().
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    mesh_size: float = 30.0
    curve_mesh_size: float = 5.0
    mapping_litho: str = "automatic_centers"
    gmsh_flag: bool = False
    merge_file: Optional[str] = None
    z_threshold: Optional[float] = None

    # Any additional keyword accepted by create_unstructured_mesh_data() can
    # be supplied here without changing this builder.
    unstructured_mesh_options: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None

    # Optional actual-coordinate overrides.  When None, the builder generates
    # them by scaling the reference Model-1 reservoir geometry.
    reservoir_extent_override: Optional[
        Tuple[float, float, float, float, float, float]
    ] = None
    fracture_planes_override: Optional[List[Tuple[float, ...]]] = None
    wells_override: Optional[List[Tuple[float, ...]]] = None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Refinement inputs
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    well_refine_size_min: float = 5.0
    well_refine_size_max: float = 30.0
    well_refine_dist_min: float = 10.0
    well_refine_dist_max: float = 60.0

    fracture_refine_size_min: float = 5.0
    fracture_refine_size_max: float = 30.0
    fracture_refine_dist_min: float = 10.0
    fracture_refine_dist_max: float = 60.0

    # If True, the six refinement lengths above are interpreted in the
    # reference 0..1000 model and scaled with the smallest model-axis scale.
    # Mesh_size and curve_mesh_size remain direct unstructured-mesh inputs.
    scale_refinement_with_model: bool = True

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Reservoir / fracture / well material inputs
    # One common material is intentionally applied to ALL 3D blocks.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    rock_porosity: float = 0.1
    rock_permeability: float = 1.0e-15
    rock_density: float = 2.6e3
    rock_thermal_conductivity: float = 3.0
    rock_heat_capacity: float = 950.0

    fracture_porosity: float = 1.0
    fracture_aperture: float = 1.0e-4

    # Geological faults already present in geomodel_result are NOT given a
    # separate fault material. They use exactly the same intrinsic rock
    # properties as the 3D reservoir. GOLEM still needs an aperture because
    # an exported geological fault is a lower-dimensional 2D FRAC block.
    geological_fault_aperture: float = 1.0

    well_porosity: float = 1.0
    well_permeability: float = 3.12e-4
    well_scaling_factor: float = 0.05

    fluid_density: float = 1.0e3
    fluid_viscosity: float = 1.0e-3
    fluid_heat_capacity: float = 4.2e3
    fluid_thermal_conductivity: float = 0.65
    fluid_modulus: float = 2.5e9

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Initial and boundary conditions
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    initial_pressure: float = 1.0e7
    initial_temperature: float = 150.0
    boundary_pressure: float = 1.0e7
    boundary_temperature: float = 150.0
    injection_temperature: float = 70.0

    # None -> use the automatically scaled reference Model-1 points.
    injection_point: Optional[Tuple[float, float, float]] = None
    extraction_point: Optional[Tuple[float, float, float]] = None

    injection_rate: float = 3.0
    extraction_rate: float = 3.0
    source_start_time: float = 0.0
    source_end_time: Optional[float] = None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Transient solve inputs
    # 19 solve times + INITIAL gives the 20 Exodus states used by Model 1.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    start_time: float = 0.0
    end_time: Optional[float] = None
    time_sequence: Optional[List[float]] = None
    automatic_scaling: bool = True
    compute_scaling_once: bool = False

    # Low-level solver controls from the working simple-reservoir input.
    coupled_petsc_options_iname: str = (
        "-ksp_type -ksp_rtol -ksp_max_it -snes_type "

    REFERENCE_MODEL_EXTENT: ClassVar[Tuple[float, ...]] = (

    )
    REFERENCE_RESERVOIR_EXTENT: ClassVar[Tuple[float, ...]] = (

    )
    REFERENCE_FRACTURE_PLANES: ClassVar[Tuple[Tuple[float, ...], ...]] = (
        (
            400.0, 450.0, 450.0,
            400.0, 550.0, 450.0,
            400.0, 550.0, 550.0,

    REFERENCE_WELLS: ClassVar[Tuple[Tuple[float, ...], ...]] = (
        (
            575.0, 500.0, 490.0,
            587.5, 500.0, 495.0,
            600.0, 500.0, 500.0,
            612.5, 500.0, 505.0,
            625.0, 500.0, 510.0,
        ),
    )
    REFERENCE_INJECTION_POINT: ClassVar[Tuple[float, float, float]] = (
        400.0, 500.0, 500.0
    )
    REFERENCE_EXTRACTION_POINT: ClassVar[Tuple[float, float, float]] = (
        600.0, 500.0, 500.0

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        self._validate_inputs()
        self._prepare_scaled_geometry()
        self._build_reservoir_mesh()
        self._classify_material_blocks()
        self._prepare_time_controls()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Geometry scaling
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _extent_tuple(extent) -> Tuple[float, float, float, float, float, float]:
        values = tuple(float(value) for value in extent)
        if len(values) != 6:
            raise ValueError("Model extent must contain 6 values: xmin,xmax,ymin,ymax,zmin,zmax")
        return values

    def _axis_scales(self) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
        ref = self.REFERENCE_MODEL_EXTENT
        dst = self.model_extent
        result = []
        for axis in range(3):
            r0, r1 = ref[2 * axis], ref[2 * axis + 1]
            d0, d1 = dst[2 * axis], dst[2 * axis + 1]
            if r1 <= r0 or d1 <= d0:
                raise ValueError("Reference and structural-model extents must have positive size")
            result.append((d1 - d0) / (r1 - r0))
        return tuple(result)

    def _scale_point(
        self, point: Tuple[float, float, float]
    ) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
        ref = self.REFERENCE_MODEL_EXTENT
        dst = self.model_extent
        out = []
        for axis, value in enumerate(point):
            r0, r1 = ref[2 * axis], ref[2 * axis + 1]
            d0, d1 = dst[2 * axis], dst[2 * axis + 1]
            fraction = (float(value) - r0) / (r1 - r0)
            out.append(d0 + fraction * (d1 - d0))
        return tuple(out)

    def _scale_extent(
        self, extent: Tuple[float, ...]
    ) -> Tuple[float, float, float, float, float, float]:
        lo = self._scale_point((extent[0], extent[2], extent[4]))
        hi = self._scale_point((extent[1], extent[3], extent[5]))
        return (lo[0], hi[0], lo[1], hi[1], lo[2], hi[2])

    def _scale_flat_xyz(self, coordinates: Tuple[float, ...]) -> Tuple[float, ...]:
        if len(coordinates) % 3:
            raise ValueError("Plane/well coordinate sequences must contain x,y,z triples")
        scaled = []
        for i in range(0, len(coordinates), 3):
            scaled.extend(self._scale_point(
                (coordinates[i], coordinates[i + 1], coordinates[i + 2])
            ))
        return tuple(scaled)

    def _prepare_scaled_geometry(self) -> None:
        self.model_extent = self._extent_tuple(
            self.geomodel_result.structural_frame.grid.extent
        )
        self.axis_scales = self._axis_scales()
        self.length_scale = min(self.axis_scales)

        self.reservoir_extent = (
            self._extent_tuple(self.reservoir_extent_override)
            if self.reservoir_extent_override is not None
            else self._scale_extent(self.REFERENCE_RESERVOIR_EXTENT)
        )

        self.fracture_planes = (
            [tuple(float(v) for v in plane) for plane in self.fracture_planes_override]
            if self.fracture_planes_override is not None
            else [
                self._scale_flat_xyz(plane)
                for plane in self.REFERENCE_FRACTURE_PLANES
            ]
        )

        self.wells = (
            [tuple(float(v) for v in well) for well in self.wells_override]
            if self.wells_override is not None
            else [
                self._scale_flat_xyz(well)
                for well in self.REFERENCE_WELLS
            ]
        )

        if self.injection_point is None:
            self.injection_point = self._scale_point(
                self.REFERENCE_INJECTION_POINT
            )
        else:
            self.injection_point = tuple(float(v) for v in self.injection_point)

        if self.extraction_point is None:
            self.extraction_point = self._scale_point(
                self.REFERENCE_EXTRACTION_POINT
            )
        else:
            self.extraction_point = tuple(float(v) for v in self.extraction_point)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Mesh generation
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _scaled_refinement_value(self, value: float) -> float:
        if self.scale_refinement_with_model:
            return float(value) * self.length_scale
        return float(value)

    def _build_reservoir_mesh(self) -> None:
        refinement = Refinement(
            wells=LinearWellRefinement(
                SizeMin=self._scaled_refinement_value(self.well_refine_size_min),
                SizeMax=self._scaled_refinement_value(self.well_refine_size_max),
                DistMin=self._scaled_refinement_value(self.well_refine_dist_min),
                DistMax=self._scaled_refinement_value(self.well_refine_dist_max),
            ),
            extraplanes=ExtraPlaneRefinement(
                SizeMin=self._scaled_refinement_value(self.fracture_refine_size_min),
                SizeMax=self._scaled_refinement_value(self.fracture_refine_size_max),
                DistMin=self._scaled_refinement_value(self.fracture_refine_dist_min),
                DistMax=self._scaled_refinement_value(self.fracture_refine_dist_max),
            ),
        )
        self.refinement = refinement

        mesh_kwargs: Dict[str, Any] = {
            "geomodel_result": self.geomodel_result,
            "extent": self.reservoir_extent,
            "wells": self.wells,
            "extra_planes": self.fracture_planes,
            "mesh_size": self.mesh_size,
            "curve_mesh_size": self.curve_mesh_size,
            "mapping_litho": self.mapping_litho,
            "refinement": refinement,
            "gmsh_flag": self.gmsh_flag,
        }
        if self.merge_file is not None:
            mesh_kwargs["merge_file"] = self.merge_file
        if self.z_threshold is not None:
            mesh_kwargs["z_threshold"] = self.z_threshold
        mesh_kwargs.update(dict(self.unstructured_mesh_options or {}))

        # Give a clear message if this WBGeo version does not expose one of the
        # requested mesh options instead of failing with a cryptic TypeError.
        signature = inspect.signature(create_unstructured_mesh_data)
        accepts_kwargs = any(
            parameter.kind == inspect.Parameter.VAR_KEYWORD
            for parameter in signature.parameters.values()
        )
        if not accepts_kwargs:
            unsupported = [
                key for key in mesh_kwargs if key not in signature.parameters
            ]
            if unsupported:
                raise ValueError(
                    "This WBGeo create_unstructured_mesh_data() version does "
                    f"not support these requested option(s): {unsupported}. "
                    f"Supported arguments are: {list(signature.parameters)}"
                )

        self.mesh_results = create_unstructured_mesh_data(**mesh_kwargs)

    def _classify_material_blocks(self) -> None:
        """Classify material blocks independently of whether the model has faults.

        WBGeo unstructured meshes append six exterior-boundary blocks. Before
        those blocks the material ordering is assumed to be:

          * structural-model 3D volume blocks,
          * optional structural-model 2D geological-fault block(s),
          * the internally-added extra-plane 2D blocks,
          * the internally-added 1D well block(s).

        The number of synthetic fracture blocks is known exactly from
        ``self.fracture_planes``. Therefore the LAST N 2D material blocks are
        the synthetic reservoir fractures and any earlier 2D blocks are
        geological faults.

        Geological faults are assigned the SAME intrinsic rock properties as
        the 3D reservoir. They remain ``material_type = FRAC`` in GOLEM only
        because a 2D element needs lower-dimensional aperture scaling.
        """
        if self.mesh_results.mesh_type != MeshType.UNSTRUCTURED:
            raise ValueError(
                "The reservoir builder must create an UNSTRUCTURED mesh"
            )
        if len(self.mesh_results.elements) <= 6:
            raise ValueError(
                "The generated unstructured mesh has no material blocks before "
                "the six WBGeo exterior-boundary blocks"
            )

        material_blocks = self.mesh_results.elements[:-6]

        self.volume_blocks = [
            i + 1 for i, block in enumerate(material_blocks) if block.dim == 3
        ]
        two_d_blocks = [
            i + 1 for i, block in enumerate(material_blocks) if block.dim == 2
        ]
        self.well_blocks = [
            i + 1 for i, block in enumerate(material_blocks) if block.dim == 1
        ]

        unsupported = [
            (i + 1, block.dim)
            for i, block in enumerate(material_blocks)
            if block.dim not in (1, 2, 3)
        ]
        if unsupported:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unsupported GOLEM material blocks (block_id, dim): {unsupported}"
            )

        n_synthetic_fractures = len(self.fracture_planes)
        if len(two_d_blocks) < n_synthetic_fractures:
            raise ValueError(
                "The generated mesh contains fewer 2D material blocks than the "
                f"{n_synthetic_fractures} internally-created fracture plane(s). "
                f"Detected 2D blocks: {two_d_blocks}"
            )

        if n_synthetic_fractures:
            self.fracture_blocks = two_d_blocks[-n_synthetic_fractures:]
            self.geological_fault_blocks = two_d_blocks[:-n_synthetic_fractures]
        else:
            self.fracture_blocks = []
            self.geological_fault_blocks = two_d_blocks

        # All blocks that use reservoir intrinsic properties. 3D blocks are
        # standard domain materials; geological_fault_blocks use a separate
        # lower-dimensional GOLEM material definition but with these same
        # rock-property values.
        self.reservoir_property_blocks = (
            list(self.volume_blocks) + list(self.geological_fault_blocks)
        )

        if not self.volume_blocks:
            raise ValueError("Generated reservoir mesh has no 3D material block")
        if not self.fracture_blocks:
            raise ValueError(
                "Generated reservoir mesh has no internally-created 2D fracture block"
            )
        if not self.well_blocks:
            raise ValueError("Generated reservoir mesh has no 1D well block")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Validation / time controls
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _validate_inputs(self) -> None:
        positive = {
            "mesh_size": self.mesh_size,
            "curve_mesh_size": self.curve_mesh_size,
            "rock_porosity": self.rock_porosity,
            "rock_permeability": self.rock_permeability,
            "rock_density": self.rock_density,
            "rock_thermal_conductivity": self.rock_thermal_conductivity,
            "rock_heat_capacity": self.rock_heat_capacity,
            "fracture_porosity": self.fracture_porosity,
            "fracture_aperture": self.fracture_aperture,
            "geological_fault_aperture": self.geological_fault_aperture,
            "well_porosity": self.well_porosity,
            "well_permeability": self.well_permeability,
            "well_scaling_factor": self.well_scaling_factor,
            "fluid_density": self.fluid_density,
            "fluid_viscosity": self.fluid_viscosity,
            "fluid_heat_capacity": self.fluid_heat_capacity,
            "fluid_thermal_conductivity": self.fluid_thermal_conductivity,
            "fluid_modulus": self.fluid_modulus,
        }
        invalid = [name for name, value in positive.items() if float(value) <= 0]
        if invalid:
            raise ValueError(
                "These simple-reservoir inputs must be > 0: " + ", ".join(invalid)
            )

    def _prepare_time_controls(self) -> None:
        if self.time_sequence is None:
            self.time_sequence = [
                1.0,
                86400.0,
                604800.0,
                2592000.0,
                7776000.0,
                15552000.0,
                31536000.0,
                63072000.0,
                126144000.0,
                315360000.0,
                630720000.0,
                946080000.0,
                1261440000.0,
                1576800000.0,
                1892160000.0,
                2207520000.0,
                2522880000.0,
                2838240000.0,
                3153600014.0,
            ]
        else:
            self.time_sequence = [float(value) for value in self.time_sequence]

        if not self.time_sequence:
            raise ValueError("time_sequence must contain at least one solve time")
        if any(t <= self.start_time for t in self.time_sequence):
            raise ValueError("Every time_sequence value must be greater than start_time")
        if any(b <= a for a, b in zip(self.time_sequence, self.time_sequence[1:])):
            raise ValueError("time_sequence values must be strictly increasing")

        if self.end_time is None:
            self.end_time = float(self.time_sequence[-1])
        if self.end_time < self.time_sequence[-1]:
            raise ValueError("end_time cannot be earlier than the final time_sequence value")

        if self.source_end_time is None:
            self.source_end_time = self.end_time
        if self.source_end_time < self.source_start_time:
            raise ValueError("source_end_time must be >= source_start_time")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # GOLEM input generation
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _point_text(point: Tuple[float, float, float]) -> str:
        if len(point) != 3:
            raise ValueError("GOLEM source points must contain exactly x, y, z")
        return " ".join(f"{float(value):.16g}" for value in point)

    @staticmethod
    def _block_text(blocks: List[int]) -> str:
        return " ".join(str(value) for value in blocks)

    def build_input_file(self, output_path: str) -> str:
        volume_blocks = self._block_text(self.volume_blocks)

    variable = temperature
    execute_on = 'INITIAL TIMESTEP_END'
    outputs = csv
  []
[]

[Preconditioning]
  [fieldsplit]
    type = FSP
    full = true
    topsplit = HT
    [HT]
      splitting = 'H T'
      splitting_type = additive
      petsc_options_iname = '{self.coupled_petsc_options_iname}'
      petsc_options_value = '{self.coupled_petsc_options_value}'
    []
    [H]
      vars = pore_pressure
      petsc_options_iname = '{self.pressure_petsc_options_iname}'
      petsc_options_value = '{self.pressure_petsc_options_value}'
    []
    [T]
      vars = temperature
      petsc_options_iname = '{self.temperature_petsc_options_iname}'
      petsc_options_value = '{self.temperature_petsc_options_value}'
    []
  []
[]

[Executioner]
  type = Transient
  solve_type = NEWTON
  start_time = {self.start_time!r}
  end_time = {self.end_time!r}
  automatic_scaling = {str(self.automatic_scaling).lower()}
  compute_scaling_once = {str(self.compute_scaling_once).lower()}
  [TimeStepper]
    type = TimeSequenceStepper
    time_sequence = '{time_sequence}'
  []
[]

[Outputs]
  print_linear_residuals = {str(self.print_linear_residuals).lower()}
  perf_graph = {str(self.perf_graph).lower()}
  print_nonlinear_converged_reason = {str(self.print_nonlinear_converged_reason).lower()}
  [exo]
    type = Exodus
    file_base = 'output/wbgeo'
    execute_on = 'INITIAL TIMESTEP_END'
  []
  [csv]
    type = CSV

[]
"""
        with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            stream.write(content)
        return output_path

docs.title: run_simulation_golem(problem, image_name, project_dir, docker_dir='/project', output_dir=None, nproc=4, keep_files_dir=None)
docs.text:
Build or copy, validate and execute a GOLEM input against a WBGeo mesh.

project_dir is bind-mounted only to expose the GOLEM executable at docker_dir/golem/golem-opt. Input and mesh files are copied into a private directory in a named container, results are copied back after the run, and the container (including its temporary directory) is removed. problem may be an automatically generated hydrothermal/simple-reservoir problem or a CustomGolemBuilder containing complete caller-supplied GOLEM input.

Source code in core/simulation_components/simulation_packages/golem/golem_run.py 
def run_simulation_golem(
    problem: Union[
        GolemHydrothermalProblemBuilder,
        GolemSimpleReservoirProblemBuilder,
        CustomGolemBuilder,
    ],
    image_name: str,
    project_dir: str,
    docker_dir: str = "/project",
    output_dir: Optional[str] = None,
    nproc: int = 4,
    keep_files_dir: Optional[str] = None,
) -> SimulationResults:
    """Build or copy, validate and execute a GOLEM input against a WBGeo mesh.

    ``project_dir`` is bind-mounted only to expose the GOLEM executable at
    ``docker_dir/golem/golem-opt``. Input and mesh files are copied into a
    private directory in a named container, results are copied back after the
    run, and the container (including its temporary directory) is removed.
    ``problem`` may be an automatically generated hydrothermal/simple-reservoir
    problem or a ``CustomGolemBuilder`` containing complete caller-supplied
    GOLEM input.
    """
    if nproc < 1:
        raise ValueError("nproc must be >= 1")
    project = Path(project_dir).resolve()
    project.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    output = Path(output_dir).resolve() if output_dir else project / "golem_output"
    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if keep_files_dir:
        run_dir = Path(keep_files_dir).resolve()
        run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        temporary = False
    else:
        run_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="golem_run_", dir=project))
        temporary = True

    container_name = f"wbgeo_golem_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}"
    container_created = False
    try:
        mesh_path = run_dir / "wbgeo_mesh.exo"
        input_path = run_dir / "wbgeo.i"
        mesh_type_code = MESH_TYPE_CODES[problem.mesh_results.mesh_type]
        exo = export_mesh_results_to_exodus(problem.mesh_results, type=mesh_type_code)
        mesh_path.write_bytes(exo.getbuffer())
        problem.build_input_file(str(input_path))

        container_run = "/tmp/wbgeo_golem_run"
        container_mesh = f"{container_run}/wbgeo_mesh.exo"
        container_input = f"{container_run}/wbgeo.i"

        generated = input_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        validate_golem_input(
            generated,
            problem.mesh_results,
            problem.mesh_results.mesh_type,
        )
        if "${GOLEM_MESH_FILE}" not in generated:
            raise ValueError("Generated GOLEM input has no ${GOLEM_MESH_FILE} placeholder")
        input_path.write_text(
            generated.replace("${GOLEM_MESH_FILE}", container_mesh), encoding="utf-8"
        )

        print(f"GOLEM host staging directory: {run_dir}", flush=True)
        print(f"Input to copy: {input_path}", flush=True)
        print(f"Mesh to copy: {mesh_path}", flush=True)
        print(f"Docker container: {container_name}", flush=True)
        print(f"MPI processes: {nproc}", flush=True)

        golem_command = (
            f'set -e; mkdir -p "{container_run}/output"; '
            f'cd "{container_run}"; '
            f'mpiexec --allow-run-as-root -n {nproc} '
            f'{docker_dir.rstrip("/")}/golem/golem-opt -i "{container_input}"'
        )
        create_command = [
            "docker", "create", "--name", container_name, "-i",
            "-v", f"{project}:{docker_dir}",
            image_name,
            "-c", golem_command,
        ]
        created = subprocess.run(
            create_command, text=True, capture_output=True, check=False
        )
        if created.returncode:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Could not create the GOLEM Docker container:\n"
                + created.stdout + created.stderr
            )
        container_created = True

        # Copy the complete staging directory so the input and mesh exist in
        # the container independently of the host bind mount.
        copied = subprocess.run(
            ["docker", "cp", str(run_dir) + "/.",
             f"{container_name}:{container_run}"],
            text=True, capture_output=True, check=False,
        )
        if copied.returncode:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Could not copy GOLEM input files into the container:\n"
                + copied.stdout + copied.stderr
            )

        transcript = _stream_process(["docker", "start", "-a", container_name])

        # Copy the ENTIRE GOLEM working directory back from the container.
        # Some MOOSE outputs (especially CSV when no file_base is given) are
        # written directly beside wbgeo.i rather than inside output/.
        container_snapshot = run_dir / "container_run"
        container_snapshot.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

        copied_back = subprocess.run(
            ["docker", "cp", f"{container_name}:{container_run}/.",
             str(container_snapshot)],
            text=True, capture_output=True, check=False,
        )
        if copied_back.returncode:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "GOLEM completed but its working directory could not be copied "
                "from Docker:\n" + copied_back.stdout + copied_back.stderr
            )

        # First preserve everything explicitly written under output/ at the
        # root of the caller's output_dir.
        staged_output = container_snapshot / "output"
        if staged_output.is_dir():
            shutil.copytree(staged_output, output, dirs_exist_ok=True)

        # Then preserve generated files/directories written directly in the
        # GOLEM working directory. Do not re-copy the staged input/mesh or the
        # output directory itself; those inputs are saved below with stable
        # WBGeo names.
        excluded_root_names = {"wbgeo.i", "wbgeo_mesh.exo", "output"}
        for item in container_snapshot.iterdir():
            if item.name in excluded_root_names:
                continue
            destination = output / item.name
            if item.is_dir():
                shutil.copytree(item, destination, dirs_exist_ok=True)
            elif item.is_file():
                shutil.copy2(item, destination)

        copied_files = sorted(
            (path for path in output.rglob("*") if path.is_file()),
            key=lambda path: str(path),
        )
        print(
            f"Copied {len(copied_files)} GOLEM output file(s) to {output}",
            flush=True,
        )
        for path in copied_files:
            print(f"  {path.relative_to(output)}", flush=True)

        # Exodus is still required to load the numerical result into WBGeo,
        # but the search below does not restrict which files are preserved.
        candidates = list(output.rglob("*.e")) + list(output.rglob("*.exo"))
        if not candidates:
            copied_listing = "\n".join(
                f"  {path.relative_to(output)}" for path in copied_files
            ) or "  <none>"
            raise RuntimeError(
                "GOLEM completed and its output files were copied, but no "
                f"Exodus result exists in {output}. Copied files:\n"
                + copied_listing
            )
        result_file = max(candidates, key=lambda path: path.stat().st_mtime)

        transcript_path = output / "golem_stdout.txt"
        transcript_path.write_text(transcript, encoding="utf-8")
        if temporary:
            # Preserve the generated inputs beside results before cleanup.
            saved_input = output / "wbgeo_generated.i"
            saved_mesh = output / "wbgeo_mesh.exo"
            shutil.copy2(input_path, saved_input)
            shutil.copy2(mesh_path, saved_mesh)
        else:
            saved_input, saved_mesh = input_path, mesh_path

        run_info = {
            "input_file": str(saved_input),
            "mesh_file": str(saved_mesh),
            "output_file": str(result_file),
            "output_dir": str(output),
            "stdout_file": str(transcript_path),
        }
        print(f"GOLEM Exodus result: {result_file}", flush=True)
        print("Loading GOLEM Exodus result into SimulationResults...", flush=True)
        simulation_results = load_exodus_results(run_info)
        if not simulation_results.nodes_by_time:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"The GOLEM Exodus file at {result_file} contained no readable time steps."
            )
        print(
            f"Loaded {len(simulation_results.nodes_by_time)} GOLEM time step(s).",
            flush=True,
        )
        return simulation_results
    finally:
        if container_created:
            removed = subprocess.run(
                ["docker", "rm", "-f", container_name],
                text=True, capture_output=True, check=False,
            )
            if removed.returncode:
                logger.warning(
                    "Could not remove temporary GOLEM container %s: %s",
                    container_name,
                    (removed.stdout + removed.stderr).strip(),
                )
        if temporary:
            shutil.rmtree(run_dir, ignore_errors=True)

docs.title: validate_golem_input(content, mesh_results, mesh_type)
docs.text:
Validate a GOLEM/MOOSE input before starting Docker.

This mirrors the structural checks used by simulation_run while accepting both modern [name] and legacy [./name] MOOSE subsection syntax, which is emitted by the GOLEM builders in this module family.

Source code in core/simulation_components/simulation_packages/golem/golem_run.py 
def validate_golem_input(content: str, mesh_results, mesh_type: MeshType) -> None:
    """Validate a GOLEM/MOOSE input before starting Docker.

    This mirrors the structural checks used by ``simulation_run`` while
    accepting both modern ``[name]`` and legacy ``[./name]`` MOOSE subsection
    syntax, which is emitted by the GOLEM builders in this module family.
    """
    required_blocks = [
        "Mesh",
        "Variables",
        "Kernels",
        "Executioner",
        "Outputs",
        "BCs",
        "Materials",
    ]
    missing = [
        block
        for block in required_blocks
        if not re.search(rf"^\s*\[{re.escape(block)}\]\s*$", content, re.MULTILINE)
    ]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError("Missing required blocks: " + ", ".join(missing))

    mesh_pattern = re.compile(
        r"""
        ^\s*\[Mesh\]\s*$
        .*?
        ^\s*type\s*=\s*FileMeshGenerator\s*$
        .*?
        ^\s*file\s*=\s*\$\{GOLEM_MESH_FILE\}\s*$
        """,
        re.DOTALL | re.MULTILINE | re.VERBOSE,
    )
    if not mesh_pattern.search(content):
        raise ValueError(
            "Mesh block must contain type = FileMeshGenerator and "
            "file = ${GOLEM_MESH_FILE}"
        )

    def extract_parent_block(text: str, parent_block: str) -> str:
        lines = text.splitlines()
        inside_parent = False
        depth = 0
        collected = []
        parent_start = f"[{parent_block}]"

        for line in lines:
            stripped = line.strip()
            if not inside_parent:
                if stripped == parent_start:
                    inside_parent = True
                continue

            if stripped == "[]":
                if depth == 0:
                    break
                depth -= 1
                collected.append(line)
                continue

            if stripped == "[../]":
                if depth > 0:
                    depth -= 1
                collected.append(line)
                continue

            if re.match(r"^\[(?:\./)?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\]$", stripped):
                depth += 1
            collected.append(line)

        return "\n".join(collected)

    def get_direct_child_blocks(text: str, parent_block: str):
        lines = text.splitlines()
        inside_parent = False
        depth = 0
        children = []
        parent_start = f"[{parent_block}]"

        for line in lines:
            stripped = line.strip()
            if not inside_parent:
                if stripped == parent_start:
                    inside_parent = True
                continue

            if stripped == "[]":
                if depth == 0:
                    break
                depth -= 1
                continue

            if stripped == "[../]":
                if depth > 0:
                    depth -= 1
                continue

            match = re.match(
                r"^\[(?:\./)?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\]$", stripped
            )
            if match:
                if depth == 0:
                    children.append(match.group(1))
                depth += 1

        return children

    materials_content = extract_parent_block(content, "Materials")
    if not materials_content.strip():
        raise ValueError("Materials block is empty")

    material_sections = get_direct_child_blocks(content, "Materials")
    if not material_sections:
        raise ValueError("No material definitions found inside the [Materials] block")

    if mesh_type == MeshType.UNSTRUCTURED:
        n_mesh_blocks = len(mesh_results.elements) - 6
    else:
        n_mesh_blocks = len(mesh_results.elements)

    if n_mesh_blocks <= 0:
        raise ValueError("The mesh has no exportable material blocks")

    # A material section does not have to correspond one-to-one with a mesh
    # block.  GolemSimpleReservoirProblemBuilder intentionally groups several
    # mesh blocks into sections such as [uniform_rock], [fractures], and [well].
    # Validate the actual block assignments instead of counting subsections.
    material_block_ids = set()
    for match in re.finditer(
        r"^\s*block\s*=\s*['\"]?([^'\"#\n]+)['\"]?\s*(?:#.*)?$",
        materials_content,
        re.MULTILINE,
    ):
        for token in match.group(1).split():
            try:
                material_block_ids.add(int(token))
            except ValueError as exc:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Invalid material block id {token!r} in [Materials]"
                ) from exc

    if not material_block_ids:
        raise ValueError(
            "No material 'block = ...' assignments found inside [Materials]"
        )

    expected_block_ids = set(range(1, n_mesh_blocks + 1))
    missing_material_ids = sorted(expected_block_ids - material_block_ids)
    extra_material_ids = sorted(material_block_ids - expected_block_ids)

    if missing_material_ids:
        raise ValueError(
            "The following mesh blocks have no material assignment: "
            + ", ".join(map(str, missing_material_ids))
        )
    if extra_material_ids:
        raise ValueError(
            "The [Materials] block references non-exportable mesh block ids: "
            + ", ".join(map(str, extra_material_ids))
        )

    variable_names = get_direct_child_blocks(content, "Variables")
    if not variable_names:
        raise ValueError("No variables found inside the [Variables] block")

    kernels_content = extract_parent_block(content, "Kernels")
    if not kernels_content.strip():
        raise ValueError("Kernels block is empty")

    kernel_variables = set(
        re.findall(
            r"^\s*variable\s*=\s*['\"]?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)['\"]?\s*$",
            kernels_content,
            re.MULTILINE,
        )
    )
    variables_without_kernel = [
        variable for variable in variable_names if variable not in kernel_variables
    ]
    if variables_without_kernel:
        raise ValueError(
            "The following variables do not have at least one kernel: "
            + ", ".join(variables_without_kernel)
        )

    logger.info(
        "GOLEM input validation successful: %d mesh blocks covered by %d material sections; variables=%s",
        n_mesh_blocks,
        len(material_sections),
        ", ".join(variable_names),
    )

docs.title: Sfepy hydrothermal builder
docs.text:
Auto-generates SfePy input file(s) for a simplified, single-phase Darcy flow + advective-conductive heat transport problem, inferring rock units and boundary regions directly from a WBGeo MeshResults + StructuralModelResults pair, instead of a hand-written static file with hardcoded regions.

This is the input-data side only: HydrothermalProblemBuilder builds the generated SfePy input files and their configuration. Actually running them (subprocess launch, output loading) lives in sfepy_hydrothermal_run.py, split out to keep "build the input data" and "run the simulation" as separate concerns -- matching the Workbench's component/connector model, where HydrothermalProblemBuilder is the input-data-generator component and run_simulation_sfepy() (sfepy_hydrothermal_run.py) is the run component.

Solved as two sequential, single-physics stages (pressure, then temperature), not one monolithic multi-field system -- see run_simulation_sfepy()'s docstring for why: solving both together in one combined linear system was tried first and turned out to be badly conditioned (pressure ~1e6 Pa and temperature ~10s of degC in the same matrix), and no amount of preconditioner tuning fixed it. Segregating matches the actual physics anyway: temperature depends on the flow field, but pressure never depends on temperature in this model.

Wired up as Workbench components in simulation_workbench_components.py (build_hydrothermal_problem, run_simulation, export_simulation_results), including a SmartInput sidebar for per-rock-unit, fluid, and fault-zone property editing (matching structural_workbench_components.py's interpolation-options pattern). build_hydrothermal_problem wraps its HydrothermalProblemBuilder in a shared SfepyProblem envelope (also defined in this file) so it and build_custom_sfepy_problem's CustomSfepyBuilder output register as the same Workbench type -- run_simulation is one component accepting either, rather than two separate Run components.

docs.title: CustomSfepyBuilder
docs.text:
Wraps a user-supplied, already-complete SfePy input file (with its own internal staging/sequencing logic -- e.g. a hand-written GOLEM-style coupled problem) instead of auto-generating one like HydrothermalProblemBuilder does. Runs through the same run_simulation_sfepy() and returns the same SimulationResults type.

input_file_contents is stored as text, not a file path: @wbgeo_type instances are serialized/reconstructed between separate Workbench component executions, and a temp file path would not survive that round trip. The content is only written to disk transiently at run time, matching how HydrothermalProblemBuilder's own generated input files work.

Validated at construction against mesh_results (known mesh type, known lithology mapping, and a best-effort static check that every 'cells of group N' the file references actually exists on the mesh -- see check_custom_sfepy_regions). This validation is deliberately not exhaustive: it cannot catch wrong material properties or malformed equations, only structural mismatches with the mesh. sfepy-run's own region resolution remains the final authority at run time.

Unlike HydrothermalProblemBuilder, no pressure/heat staging, no velocity handoff -- the file is assumed to already contain everything it needs and gets run in a single sfepy-run invocation (see run_simulation_sfepy in sfepy_hydrothermal_run.py). On an unstructured mesh, the same mesh_type_code == "unstr" pre-filter HydrothermalProblemBuilder relies on (_run_sfepy_input_file, dropping non-volume blocks before Exodus export) applies here too -- so a custom file cannot reference a non-volume (fault-surface/boundary) block by group number on an unstructured mesh, the same limitation HydrothermalProblemBuilder already has. mesh_results with any well/source (dim < 2) block is rejected outright at construction (see check_mesh_has_no_engineering_objects) -- not supported yet.

fault_zone_n_voxels: optional opt-in for a "damage zone" cell selection, the same mechanism HydrothermalProblemBuilder uses (see compute_fault_zone_cell_mask) -- a band of cells straddling each active fault's trace gets reassigned its own group id (self.fault_group_id), referenceable from the custom file as 'cells of group {fault_group_id}' (e.g. as its own 'Omega_fault' region). Unlike HydrothermalProblemBuilder, no material/equation is auto-generated for this group -- the custom file's author decides what to do with it; this only provides the cell selection. Requires geomodel_result (raises if not given). None (default) leaves the mesh's real lithology groups as the only ones available, exactly like today.

Source code in core/simulation_components/simulation_packages/sfepy/sfepy_hydrothermal_builder.py 
@wbgeo_type(name='Custom SfePy Problem', color='#e07a5f', identifier='CustomSfepyBuilder')
@dataclass
class CustomSfepyBuilder:
    """
    Wraps a user-supplied, already-complete SfePy input file (with its own
    internal staging/sequencing logic -- e.g. a hand-written GOLEM-style
    coupled problem) instead of auto-generating one like
    HydrothermalProblemBuilder does. Runs through the same
    run_simulation_sfepy() and returns the same SimulationResults type.

    input_file_contents is stored as text, not a file path: @wbgeo_type
    instances are serialized/reconstructed between separate Workbench
    component executions, and a temp file path would not survive that
    round trip. The content is only written to disk transiently at run
    time, matching how HydrothermalProblemBuilder's own generated input
    files work.

    Validated at construction against mesh_results (known mesh type,
    known lithology mapping, and a best-effort static check that every
    'cells of group N' the file references actually exists on the mesh --
    see check_custom_sfepy_regions). This validation is deliberately not
    exhaustive: it cannot catch wrong material properties or malformed
    equations, only structural mismatches with the mesh. sfepy-run's own
    region resolution remains the final authority at run time.

    Unlike HydrothermalProblemBuilder, no pressure/heat staging, no
    velocity handoff -- the file is assumed to already contain everything
    it needs and gets run in a single sfepy-run invocation (see
    run_simulation_sfepy in sfepy_hydrothermal_run.py). On an unstructured
    mesh, the same mesh_type_code == "unstr" pre-filter
    HydrothermalProblemBuilder relies on (_run_sfepy_input_file, dropping
    non-volume blocks before Exodus export) applies here too -- so a
    custom file cannot reference a non-volume (fault-surface/boundary)
    block by group number on an unstructured mesh, the same limitation
    HydrothermalProblemBuilder already has. mesh_results with any
    well/source (dim < 2) block is rejected outright at construction (see
    check_mesh_has_no_engineering_objects) -- not supported yet.

    fault_zone_n_voxels: optional opt-in for a "damage zone" cell
    selection, the same mechanism HydrothermalProblemBuilder uses (see
    compute_fault_zone_cell_mask) -- a band of cells straddling each
    active fault's trace gets reassigned its own group id
    (self.fault_group_id), referenceable from the custom file as
    'cells of group {fault_group_id}' (e.g. as its own 'Omega_fault'
    region). Unlike HydrothermalProblemBuilder, no material/equation is
    auto-generated for this group -- the custom file's author decides
    what to do with it; this only provides the cell selection. Requires
    geomodel_result (raises if not given). None (default) leaves the
    mesh's real lithology groups as the only ones available, exactly like
    today.
    """
    input_file_contents: str
    mesh_results: MeshResults
    geomodel_result: Optional[StructuralModelResults] = None
    fault_zone_n_voxels: Optional[int] = None
    print_linear_residuals: bool = False

    def __post_init__(self):
        check_mesh_has_known_type(self.mesh_results)
        check_mesh_has_no_engineering_objects(self.mesh_results)
        check_mesh_has_lithology_mapping(self.mesh_results)
        self.mesh_type = self.mesh_results.mesh_type
        self.mat_id_to_lithology = map_mat_id_to_lithology(self.mesh_results)

        self.fault_zone_cell_mask: Optional[np.ndarray] = None
        self.fault_group_id: Optional[int] = None
        if self.fault_zone_n_voxels is not None:
            if self.geomodel_result is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    "fault_zone_n_voxels was given but geomodel_result is None -- "
                    "computing the fault-zone cell mask needs the structural model."
                )
            self.fault_zone_cell_mask = compute_fault_zone_cell_mask(
                self.mesh_results, self.geomodel_result, self.fault_zone_n_voxels,
            )
            if self.fault_zone_cell_mask is not None:
                self.fault_group_id = len(self.mesh_results.elements)

        check_custom_sfepy_regions(
            self.input_file_contents, self.mesh_results,
            extra_valid_groups={self.fault_group_id} if self.fault_group_id is not None else set(),
        )
        if self.geomodel_result is not None:
            n_referenced = len(extract_referenced_groups(self.input_file_contents))
            n_lithologies = len(enumerate_rock_units(self.geomodel_result))
            if n_referenced < n_lithologies:
                logger.warning(
                    "File references %d group(s) via 'cells of group N' but the "
                    "structural model defines %d lithologies -- expected if a "
                    "lithology is split across disconnected mesh blocks (e.g. a "
                    "fault), otherwise the file may be missing coverage.",
                    n_referenced, n_lithologies,
                )

Bases: BaseModel

Canonical fluid properties shared by the SfePy and GOLEM builders.

Source code in core/simulation_components/simulation_packages/sfepy/sfepy_hydrothermal_builder.py 
class FluidProperties(BaseModel):
    """Canonical fluid properties shared by the SfePy and GOLEM builders."""
    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True)

    mu: float = Field(
        1.0e-3, validation_alias=AliasChoices("mu", "viscosity")
    )
    k_fluid: float = Field(
        0.6,
        validation_alias=AliasChoices("k_fluid", "thermal_conductivity"),
    )
    density: float = 1000.0                   # kg/m^3
    heat_capacity: Optional[float] = None     # J/(kg*K)
    rho_c_fluid: Optional[float] = None       # J/(m^3*K)
    fluid_modulus: float = 2.2e9              # Pa

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def calculate_volumetric_heat_capacity(self) -> "FluidProperties":
        if self.mu <= 0 or self.k_fluid <= 0 or self.density <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                "fluid viscosity, thermal conductivity and density must be > 0"
            )
        if self.heat_capacity is None and self.rho_c_fluid is None:
            self.rho_c_fluid = 4.186e6
            self.heat_capacity = self.rho_c_fluid / self.density
        elif self.heat_capacity is None:
            self.heat_capacity = float(self.rho_c_fluid) / self.density
        elif self.rho_c_fluid is None:
            self.rho_c_fluid = self.density * self.heat_capacity
        elif not np.isclose(
            self.rho_c_fluid,
            self.density * self.heat_capacity,
            rtol=1.0e-10,
            atol=0.0,
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                "rho_c_fluid must equal density * heat_capacity"
            )
        if self.heat_capacity <= 0:
            raise ValueError("fluid heat_capacity must be > 0")
        return self

    @property
    def viscosity(self) -> float:
        return self.mu

    @property
    def thermal_conductivity(self) -> float:
        return self.k_fluid

Builds SfePy problem-description files for a coupled Darcy flow + heat transport problem, solved as two sequential single-physics stages. Material regions and boundary regions are inferred automatically from the mesh and structural model.

Temperature is coupled to the Darcy flow: pressure is solved first, a Darcy velocity is computed from its gradient, and that velocity enters the temperature equation as a dw_advect_div_free advection term.

Set include_flow=False to skip the pressure stage entirely and solve pure heat conduction instead -- useful to validate the diffusion term in isolation (e.g. against the known analytical steady-state profile) before trusting the coupled result. Rock units still use porosity-weighted effective conductivity/heat capacity by default in this mode (a static, saturated rock); to also remove the fluid's contribution entirely, set porosity=0.0 on the relevant RockUnitProperties -- the same formulas then reduce exactly to k_solid/rho_c_solid.

mesh_type (which meshing component produced mesh_results -- one of MeshType.IMPLICIT/STRUCTURED/UNSTRUCTURED) is read directly from mesh_results.mesh_type, set automatically by create_implicit_structured_mesh/create_structured_mesh_data/ create_unstructured_mesh_data -- not a separate constructor argument, since that would just be a second place the same fact could go stale or disagree with the actual mesh. Raises clearly if mesh_results.mesh_type is None (e.g. a manually-constructed MeshResults in a test that never set it). All three mesh types work end-to-end for unfaulted models; a structured mesh paired with a faulted structural model is not supported (blocked at the meshing stage, since that combination does not reliably converge -- use implicit or unstructured meshing for faulted models instead).

Limited fault support: pass fault_zone_properties (a RockUnitProperties) to give cells near any fault their own separate material, instead of silently treating them as ordinary lithology. Off by default (None). Faults aren't tagged anywhere on MeshResults for implicit/structured meshes (only a per-block lithology id); only unstructured meshing explicitly meshes fault surfaces, and SfePy itself has no fault/interface element either (only per-region material constants, same as lithology already uses) -- so this represents a fault as a "damage zone" band of cells straddling its trace (fault_zone_n_voxels grid cells wide, computed on the structural model's grid via each fault's get_domain_mask(), then resampled to mesh cells the same way lithology is resampled for unstructured meshes), a standard, simpler proxy for fault hydraulics (gouge seal or fracture-enhanced conduit) than an exact geometric split. All faults in the structural model are combined into one shared "fault zone" material region (Omega_fault) -- not per-fault -- deliberately the smallest useful increment, not a complete fault model. Respects structural_frame.fault_activity though: the structural modeling component supports finite faults that don't cut every stratigraphic group (model9 is the clearest example; a single fault can also be restricted this way via set_fault_activity_by_index/_by_group), and a fault's raw get_domain_mask() doesn't know about that restriction at all (it's a purely geometric scalar_field > scalar_value quantity) -- so the fault-zone trace is masked, per fault, to only the grid cells whose lithology's stratigraphic group that fault is actually active for (group_idx >= fault_activity[name], the same rule effective_domain_components_for_group in general.py uses for the real lith_block computation; basement is always treated as active, since it sits below/outside every group). Setting fault_zone_properties identical to the surrounding rock's properties is a no-op on the result (useful for isolating a suspected fault-zone effect by comparison).
